qa_pairs.instruction: What is the purpose of importing the latest Linux and Unix driver packages before installing the driver?
qa_pairs.output: Importing the latest Linux and Unix driver packages ensures that the Package Catalog contains the most recent configuration and feature updates, which is required before you can install the Linux and Unix driver and guarantee it operates with current functionality.

qa_pairs.instruction: How do you import the current Linux and Unix driver packages into the Package Catalog using Designer?
qa_pairs.output:
1. Open Designer.
2. In the toolbar, choose Help > Check for Package Updates.
3. Click **OK** if there are no updates, or click **OK** to import updates.
4. In the Outline view, right‑click **Package Catalog** and select **Import Package**.
5. In the Import Package dialog, select **Linux and Unix Packages** (or click **Select All** to import every displayed package).
6. If only base packages are shown, deselect **Show Base Packages Only** to see all packages.
7. Click **OK** to import the selected packages, then click **OK** again in the successful import message.
8. After the packages are imported, proceed to install the driver.

qa_pairs.instruction: How do you install the Linux and Unix driver packages and select optional features in Designer?
qa_pairs.output:
1. In Designer, open your project.
2. In the Modeler, right‑click the driver set where you want the driver and choose **New > Driver**.
3. Select **Linux and Unix Base** from the list of base packages and click **Next**.
4. On the optional features screen, select the packages you need (Default Configuration, Entitlements, Password Synchronization, Data Collection, Account Tracking) and click **Next**.
5. If any selected package has dependencies, click **OK** to install them; repeat for additional dependencies if prompted.
6. Fill in any displayed Common Settings pages, then continue through the remaining wizard pages, providing required information, and finish by clicking **Finish**.

qa_pairs.instruction: What optional feature packages can be selected when installing the Linux and Unix driver, and what does each provide?
qa_pairs.output:
• **Default Configuration** – Contains the default configuration information for the Linux and Unix driver; always leave selected.
• **Entitlements** – Provides configuration for synchronizing Linux and Unix accounts and policies that enable account creation and auditing.
• **Password Synchronization** – Contains policies that enable the Linux and Unix driver to synchronize passwords.
• **Data Collection** – Includes policies that enable the driver to collect data for reports (used with the Identity Reporting Module).
• **Account Tracking** – Includes policies that enable tracking of accounts for reports (used with the Identity Reporting Module).

qa_pairs.instruction: Which fields must be filled on the Common Settings page when installing the Linux and Unix driver, and what do they represent?
qa_pairs.output:
• **User Container** – The Identity Vault container where Linux and Unix user objects will be added if they do not already exist; this becomes the default for all drivers in the driver set.
• **Group Container** – Not applicable for the Linux and Unix driver because it does not synchronize Group objects; this setting can be ignored.

qa_pairs.instruction: What information is required on the Common Settings Advanced Edition page for the Linux and Unix driver?
qa_pairs.output:
• **User Application Provisioning Services URL** – The URL of the User Application Identity Manager Provisioning service.
• **User Application Provisioning Services Administrator** – The distinguished name (DN) of the User Application Administrator user who has rights to create and assign resources.

qa_pairs.instruction: What Remote Loader connection parameters must be set on the Install Linux and Unix Base page for the Linux and Unix driver?
qa_pairs.output:
• **Connect to Remote Loader** – Must be set to **Yes** to use the Remote Loader.
• **Host Name** – Specify the host (or port number) where the Remote Loader is installed and running; the default port is **8090**.
• **Port** – Specify the Remote Loader’s password as defined on the Remote Loader.
• **Remote Password** – Also specify the Remote Loader’s password (same value as the Port field).
• **Driver Password** – Specify the driver object password defined in the Remote Loader service.

qa_pairs.instruction: What classification and environment options can be selected on the Managed System Information page for the Linux and Unix driver?
qa_pairs.output:
• **Classification** options: Mission‑Critical, Vital, Not‑Critical, Other (requires a custom classification when selected).
• **Environment** options: Development, Test, Staging, Production, Other (requires a custom classification when selected).

qa_pairs.instruction: What fields are required on the System Ownership page for the Linux and Unix driver?
qa_pairs.output:
• **Business Owner** – Choose a user object in the Identity Vault who is the business owner of the Linux and Unix system (must be a user, not a role, group, or container).
• **Application Owner** – Choose a user object in the Identity Vault who is the application owner of the Linux and Unix system (must be a user, not a role, group, or container).

qa_pairs.instruction: What fields must be completed on the General Information page for the Linux and Unix driver?
qa_pairs.output:
• **Name** – Descriptive name for the Linux and Unix system (appears in reports).
• **Description** – Brief description of the Linux and Unix system (appears in reports).
• **Location** – Physical location of the Linux and Unix system (appears in reports).
• **Vendor** – Vendor of the Linux and Unix system (appears in reports).
• **Version** – Version of the Linux and Unix system (appears in reports).

qa_pairs.instruction: What fields are required on the Entitlements Name to CSV File Mappings page for the Linux and Unix driver?
qa_pairs.output:
• **Entitlement Name** – Descriptive name for the entitlement that maps to the CSV file (corresponds to the Entitlement Assignment Attribute in Linux and Unix).
• **Entitlement Assignment Attribute** – Name of the attribute that holds entitlement values in Linux and Unix.
• **CSV File** – Path to the CSV file on the same server as the driver that contains entitlement values.
• **Multi‑valued?** – Set to **True** to allow assigning resources and entitlements multiple times with different values to the same user; set to **False** otherwise.

qa_pairs.instruction: How can you access and modify the driver properties for the Linux and Unix driver after it has been created?
qa_pairs.output:
1. Open your project in Designer.
2. In the Modeler, right‑click the Linux and Unix driver icon (or the driver line) and select **Properties**.
3. On the Driver Properties page, modify the driver settings, Driver Parameters, Global Configuration Values, or any other configuration as needed, then save your changes.

qa_pairs.instruction: How do you deploy the Linux and Unix driver to the Identity Vault using Designer?
qa_pairs.output:
1. In Designer, open your project.
2. In the Modeler, right‑click the Linux and Unix driver icon (or the driver line) and choose **Live > Deploy**.
3. If not already authenticated, provide the Identity Vault **Host**, **Username** (DN), and **Password**, then click **OK**.
4. Review the deployment summary and click **Deploy**.
5. After a successful deployment message, click **OK**.
6. Click **Define Security Equivalence** to assign rights to the driver (add a user object with the required rights and click **OK** twice).
7. Click **Exclude Administrative Roles** to prevent administrative user objects from being synchronized (add each object to exclude and click **OK** for each, then click **OK**).
8. Click **OK** to finish the deployment.

qa_pairs.instruction: How do you assign security equivalence and exclude administrative roles when deploying the Linux and Unix driver?
qa_pairs.output:
1. After deploying the Linux and Unix driver, click **Define Security Equivalence**.
2. Click **Add**, browse to the user object that should have the same rights as the driver (e.g., Admin or DriversUser), select it, and click **OK** twice.
3. Click **Exclude Administrative Roles**.
4. Click **Add**, browse to each administrative user object you want to exclude (e.g., Admin, DriversUser), select it, and click **OK**.
5. Repeat step 4 for each object to exclude, then click **OK** to confirm.

qa_pairs.instruction: How do you start the Linux and Unix driver after it has been deployed?
qa_pairs.output:
1. In Designer, open your project.
2. In the Modeler, right‑click the Linux and Unix driver icon (or the driver line) and select **Live > Start Driver**.

qa_pairs.instruction: Summarize the end‑to‑end process for creating, configuring, deploying, and starting the Linux and Unix driver in Designer.
qa_pairs.output: To create a Linux and Unix driver, first import the latest Linux and Unix packages into the Package Catalog. Then install the driver packages, selecting optional features such as Entitlements and Password Synchronization, and complete any required Common Settings, Remote Loader connection details, and Managed System Information fields. After the driver is created, modify its properties as needed, deploy it to the Identity Vault (providing Vault credentials if required), assign security equivalence, and exclude administrative accounts. Finally, start the driver via Live > Start Driver to make it operational.
